terminal_record.title: Trump Pardoned William E. Henry on January 19, 2021
terminal_record.description_short: Trump pardoned William E. Henry on January 19, 2021, for a federal theft-of-government-property conviction.
terminal_record.description_medium: The Justice Department lists William E. Henry under January 19, 2021 pardons, with the Middle District of Alabama, theft of government property, and a sentence of two years’ probation plus a $4,000 fine dated May 2, 2019. The listing does not state Trump’s reason for granting clemency.
terminal_record.description_long: On January 19, 2021, Donald Trump granted a pardon to William E. Henry, whom the Department of Justice Office of the Pardon Attorney lists under that date. The official table names Henry, identifies the Middle District of Alabama, and lists theft of government property as the offense. It records two years’ probation and a $4,000 fine, with the sentence dated May 2, 2019. Those entries document the person, federal district, offense label, and sentence associated with the clemency grant. The table does not explain why Trump selected Henry, describe the conduct behind the conviction, or report an exchange or other private benefit. The fact of a pardon alone does not establish a corrupt motive. Accordingly, this entry describes a documented presidential pardon while leaving motive and underlying case facts unknown. No exchange, financial loss, political favoritism, or public reaction is documented in the DOJ table.

terminal_record.title: Trump and Hegseth Remove Senior Military Leaders in February 2025
terminal_record.description_short: Trump fired Joint Chiefs Chair C.Q. Brown; Hegseth also dismissed senior officers. The supplied impeachment-retaliation motive remains unsupported.
terminal_record.description_medium: On February 21, 2025, President Donald Trump fired Joint Chiefs Chairman Air Force Gen. C.Q. Brown Jr. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth then fired Navy Adm. Lisa Franchetti and Air Force Gen. James Slife, according to AP reporting. Reuters described Brown and five other admirals and generals as pushed out in the leadership shake-up. The supplied impeachment-testimony motive is not established by these sources and is omitted from this corrected account.
terminal_record.description_long: This corrected entry records a February 2025 change in senior U.S. military leadership. Reuters reported that President Donald Trump fired Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen. C.Q. Brown on February 21 and described five other admirals and generals as pushed out in the same shake-up. The Associated Press reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth followed Brown’s dismissal by firing Navy Adm. Lisa Franchetti, then chief of naval operations, and Air Force Gen. James Slife, vice chief of the Air Force; AP also reported on changes to the services’ top military lawyers. The supplied record asserted that officers were removed because they testified against Trump in impeachment proceedings. The reporting reviewed for this corrected card documents who was dismissed, but does not establish that causal allegation or identify impeachment testimony as the reason. The account therefore names only the documented personnel actions and leaves motive unresolved. It does not characterize the changes as retaliation, a purge of witnesses, or proof of political loyalty. No conclusion about legality or resulting readiness effects is drawn. This correction preserves the dated leadership-change event while removing unsupported participants and motive.
